answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities with earned throughput: a new identity starts able to take only one small verified job at a time, and its capacity grows only after each job is attested by unrelated peers, like a delta widening one channel at a time. A yarrow plant spreads slowly from a single root, and likewise standing cannot be transplanted or bought in bulk. A plume of new identities each stays throttled at the minimum, so an attacker needing volume must wait through each identity's history in sequence, and total fake throughput stays capped no matter how many names are created.
